requirement_vague: Verify comment creation adds comment to article and can be retrieved
requirement_precise: Create a user (username: 'commentuser1', email: 'commentuser1@test.com', password: 'pass123'). Create an article with title 'Comment Test Article'. Extract the slug. Create a comment on the article via POST /api/articles/{slug}/comments with body 'This is my test comment'. Verify response status is 200. Verify the response article has comments array with length >= 1. GET the comments for the article via GET /api/articles/{slug}/comments. Verify status 200. Verify the comments array contains a comment with body 'This is my test comment'. Verify the comment has an 'id' field that is a number.

implementation.reasoning: The POST comment endpoint persists a Comment linked to the target article via article_id and returns the article with include_comments=True, which adds a comments array containing each comment including numeric id and body. The GET comments endpoint retrieves comments for the article and returns them in a comments array, so the created comment body can be fetched afterward with HTTP 200.
